title: No removable-media replication observed; D:/F: volume writes are fixed-disk DFSR and pagefile activity
summary: The T1091 hypothesis is not supported. The only file-creation events on non-C: drive letters in windows.sysmon are (a) 14 writes by C:\windows\system32\DFSRs.exe to F:\System Volume Information\DFSR\Config\*.XML.TMP on newyork.dmevals.local between 02:56:48Z and 03:26:49Z, which is normal DFS Replication staging on a fixed volume, and (b) one write of D:\pagefile.sys by C:\windows\System32\smss.exe on scranton.dmevals.local at 03:19:09Z, which is normal pagefile creation at boot. windows.other volume-health events (code 98) confirm C:, D: and \\?\Volume{d1b3f076-...} are \Device\HarddiskVolume* fixed disks, not removable media. No USB device, removable-volume or drive-letter insertion events were found in windows.other, and the Sysinternals Volumeid.exe files seen on scranton were written to C:\Users\pbeesly\Downloads, not to removable media. The Zeek dataset (2020-04-30) does not overlap the Windows window and contains no removable-media telemetry.

title: No remote service session hijacking observed; lateral movement used PsExec service execution instead
summary: Hunting for T1563 (Remote Service Session Hijacking) produced no hijack evidence. The only remote-interactive (LogonType 10) logons in the window are two 4624 events on scranton.dmevals.local at 2020-05-02T03:20:46Z for DMEVALS\pbeesly from 172.18.39.2 (LogonProcessName 'User32 ', WorkstationName SCRANTON, TargetLogonId 0x1305dc, Linked Logon ID 0x13069A). That session is a normal, freshly established RDP logon: TermService (svchost -k NetworkService -s TermService) spawned rdpclip.exe at 03:20:48Z in TerminalSessionId 2 with LogonId 0x13069A, followed by explorer.exe, LogonUI.exe, dwm.exe and fontdrvhost.exe — i.e. a new interactive desktop, not a takeover of an existing session. No tscon, mstsc, qwinsta or query session execution exists in sysmon process-creation events, and the 120 PowerShell 4104 'hits' for tscon/qwinsta/query session are false positives from built-in CimCmdlets module text (e.g. '[Alias('Session')] [CimSession[]] ${CimSession}') on newyork.dmevals.local, not attacker script. The real lateral movement in this window is PsExec-based (T1021.002), which is outside this technique family.

title: RDP session on scranton is a legitimate new interactive logon, not a hijacked session
summary: The single RDP-related network event is a sysmon event.code 3 on scranton.dmevals.local at 2020-05-02T03:20:21Z: svchost.exe (PID 1056, NT AUTHORITY\NETWORK SERVICE) receiving an inbound TCP connection from 172.18.39.2:60579 to 10.0.1.4:3389 (Initiated: false). It is immediately followed by the LogonType 10 4624 for pbeesly from 172.18.39.2 and by rdpclip.exe spawned from TermService in TerminalSessionId 2. There is no evidence of session takeover: no tscon.exe execution (C119 zero hits), no mstsc/ssh/winrs command lines (C114 zero hits), no Enter-PSSession/New-PSSession script blocks (C116 zero hits), and no second session being redirected to an existing one. The RDP session is the attacker's/user's own interactive foothold on scranton, from which the actual lateral movement to nashua.dmevals.local was performed with PsExec64.exe (cleartext -u dmevals\pbeesly -p ... \\NASHUA -i 2 C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe at 03:11:18Z, 03:12:25Z, 03:13:28Z, 03:14:42Z), creating PSEXESVC services and running python.exe on nashua — that is T1021.002, not RDP hijacking.

title: SYSVOL/IPC$ share access by machine accounts (NEWYORK$, SCRANTON$) — benign domain replication traffic
summary: The remaining 5140/5145 share hits are SYSVOL and IPC$ access by machine accounts: NEWYORK$ from fe80::e40c:95b6:b0a7:6429 and SCRANTON$ from 10.0.1.4 on newyork.dmevals.local, plus IPC$ sessions. These are read-oriented domain controller replication/Group Policy and SMB session setup patterns (SYSVOL share path \\??\F:\SYSVOL\sysvol), not tool staging. No file writes to ADMIN$ or other hosts were observed from these accounts, so they are assessed as normal domain behaviour rather than lateral tool transfer.

title: PowerShell Invoke-Exfil script on SCRANTON copies archive to remote WebDAV share
summary: On scranton.dmevals.local, user pbeesly executed a script block (4104, ScriptBlock ID b2b03a9c-43f0-4285-837d-f22d4600b2ae, path C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\psversion.ps1) defining Invoke-Exfil: it installs 7Zip4Powershell, compresses the user's Downloads folder into %APPDATA%\OfficeSupplies.7z with password 'lolol', maps a drive to \\192.168.0.4\webdav using hardcoded credentials (cozy / MyCozyPassw0rd!) and Copy-Item's the archive there. This is file transfer to a remote share, but the direction is outbound staging/exfiltration rather than moving tools onto a victim host, so it is recorded as suspicious supporting context for the same actor on the same host rather than a T1570 tool-transfer instance.

summary: On 2020-05-02 between 03:04:04 and 03:20:46 NEWYORK.dmevals.local recorded six LogonType 3 (network) logons for DMEVALS\pbeesly, five sourced from 10.0.1.4 (SCRANTON, the compromised host) and one from 10.0.1.6 (NASHUA, the already-compromised second host). The 03:04:04 logon (logon id 0x5dd594, Kerberos, source port 59900) was immediately followed by a 5140 network-share access to \\*\IPC$ by pbeesly from 10.0.1.4 — the same pattern as the PsExec ADMIN$ activity against NASHUA, but against the domain controller. No process creation, service install or file write by pbeesly was observed on NEWYORK in this window, so this is SMB/remote-access reconnaissance or an attempted remote execution that did not complete in the captured data.
title: pbeesly network logons to NEWYORK (DC) from SCRANTON 10.0.1.4 with IPC$ access — SMB lateral movement beyond NASHUA

summary: On NASHUA.dmevals.local the attacker-written C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe (dropped via PsExec) wrote C:\Windows\Temp\Rar.exe at 03:15:31 and C:\Windows\Temp\sdelete64.exe at 03:15:38, then spawned powershell.exe (03:15:48) which ran Rar.exe to create C:\Users\pbeesly\Desktop\working.zip (03:16:19) and cmd.exe (03:16:40) which ran sdelete64.exe against Rar.exe, working.zip in Roaming and Desktop. This is tool staging/transfer onto the victim host plus anti-forensic cleanup, distinct from the PSEXESVC.exe/python.exe drops already anchored.
title: Tool transfer onto NASHUA: python.exe, Rar.exe and sdelete64.exe written to C:\Windows\Temp and executed

summary: NASHUA recorded LogonType 2 (interactive) logons for pbeesly at 03:11:40, 03:12:46, 03:13:49 and 03:15:03, each within ~20 seconds of a LogonType 3 network logon from 10.0.1.4 (SCRANTON) and of a PSEXESVC.exe service start plus C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe launch. This is the interactive-session side effect of the PsExec -i 2 remote execution, i.e. remote interactive access to NASHUA driven from the compromised SCRANTON host.
title: pbeesly interactive (LogonType 2) sessions on NASHUA following each PsExec network logon
